children.title: Distributed Optimization Metrics and Stopping Criteria
children.top_down_role: Observable optimization, agreement, feasibility, and saddle-progress measures.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\) be distributed primal states, possibly accompanied by dual variables \(Y\), and let \(\mathcal T\) be the target solution set. Let \(Z=(X,Y,\xi)\) denote all locally held state and auxiliary transcript information available to a certification procedure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition covers optimization, agreement, feasibility, stationarity, and saddle-progress certificates; computability and soundness are separated from completeness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed accuracy certificate is a nonnegative observable map \(C:Z\mapsto[0,\infty]\) together with a target error map \(E:Z\mapsto[0,\infty]\) and a nondecreasing calibration \(\psi\) satisfying \(\psi(0)=0\), such that \(C(Z)\le\varepsilon\) implies \(E(Z)\le\psi(\varepsilon)\) for every admissible instance and state. The certificate is exact when \(C(Z)=0\) if and only if the certified primal-dual state belongs to \(\mathcal T\). It is distributedly evaluable when agents can compute or upper-bound \(C(Z)\) using the declared local observations and a finite specified aggregation protocol.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributed accuracy certificate is an observable nonnegative quantity whose small value guarantees a small true target error. Its calibration states precisely what accuracy follows from a threshold. Exactness means that zero certificate value characterizes the target solution set. Distributed evaluability requires an explicit finite protocol using available local information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall Z\ \forall\varepsilon\ge0:\quad C(Z)\le\varepsilon\Longrightarrow E(Z)\le\psi(\varepsilon),\qquad \psi(0)=0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A vector certificate \((C_{\mathrm{opt}},C_{\mathrm{con}},C_{\mathrm{feas}},C_{\mathrm{stat}})\) may be scalarized as \(C=\max_j C_j/\eta_j\) for declared positive tolerances \(\eta_j\).
special_cases_latex: For consensus optimization, a certificate may combine objective suboptimality at an aggregate state with \(\max_i\|x_i-\bar x\|\), provided both terms are observable or validly upper-bounded.
For a convex-concave saddle problem, a restricted primal-dual gap can serve as \(C\) on the declared bounded test sets.
immediate_consequences_latex: A stopping rule \(C(Z^k)\le\varepsilon\) is sound for the calibrated target error.
Certificate evaluation itself may consume communication and must be included in complexity accounting when non-negligible.
boundary_notes: Objective error involving an unknown optimum value is not directly observable unless a computable bound or dual certificate is supplied.
A small consensus residual alone does not certify optimality, and a small local stationarity residual alone need not certify agreement or feasibility.
Completeness, meaning that every accurate state has a small certificate, is an additional property not implied by soundness.

notation.meaning: True target error controlled by the certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: Sound observable distributed accuracy certificate

assumptions_latex: \(F=f+r\), where \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable and \(r:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The stepsize satisfies \(\eta>0\), the point satisfies \(x\in\operatorname{dom}r\), and the proximal map of \(r\) is exactly evaluable.
The stationarity tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|G_\eta(x)\|_2\le\varepsilon\), with \(G_\eta(x)=0\Longleftrightarrow0\in\nabla f(x)+\partial r(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal-gradient residual certificate for unconstrained smooth-plus-convex composite optimization.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F=f+r\) and \(\eta>0\), define \[G_\eta(x)=\frac1\eta\left(x-\operatorname{prox}_{\eta r}(x-\eta\nabla f(x))\right).\] A point \(x\in\operatorname{dom}r\), together with the evaluated gradient and proximal point, is an \(\varepsilon\)-composite-stationarity certificate if \[\|G_\eta(x)\|_2\le\varepsilon.\] The exact-zero relation is \[G_\eta(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad0\in\nabla f(x)+\partial r(x).\] For a distributed finite sum, the gradient in the mapping must be the aggregated gradient evaluated at the reported common point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small proximal-gradient mapping certifies approximate composite stationarity, and a zero mapping is equivalent to the composite first-order condition.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be nonempty, let \(F:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), let \(F_\star=\inf_{x\in X}F(x)>-\infty\), and let \(z\) denote the distributed state from which a candidate \(x(z)\in X\) is decoded.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic minimization; the definition separates optimization progress from consensus and constraint-feasibility errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An optimization-progress certificate system is a map \(C_{\mathrm{opt}}:\mathcal Z\to[0,+\infty]\), together with a declared tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\ge0\), such that \(C_{\mathrm{opt}}(z)\) is computable from the admitted state information and \(C_{\mathrm{opt}}(z)\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\) implies a specified optimization condition. Canonical choices are the objective certificate \(C_{\mathrm{obj}}(z)=F(x(z))-F_\star\) and, when \(F\) is differentiable on an open neighborhood of \(X\), the stationarity certificate \(C_{\mathrm{stat}}(z)=\operatorname{dist}(0,\nabla F(x(z))+N_X(x(z)))\). The certificate is exact when \(C_{\mathrm{opt}}(z)=0\) holds exactly at globally optimal points for the objective form, or at first-order stationary points for the stationarity form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimization-progress certificate assigns a nonnegative residual to a distributed state and declares progress adequate when that residual is below a tolerance. The objective-gap form is the decoded candidate's objective value minus the optimal value. The stationarity form is the distance from zero to the gradient plus the feasible-set normal cone. Zero objective gap characterizes global optimality, whereas zero stationarity residual characterizes first-order stationarity in the stated smooth constrained regime. Consensus and feasibility violations are not included unless explicitly incorporated into the chosen residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_{\mathrm{opt}}(z)\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\) is the declared optimization-progress certificate, with the certified property determined by the selected residual.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For unconstrained smooth minimization, \(X=\mathbb R^d\) gives \(C_{\mathrm{stat}}(z)=\|\nabla F(x(z))\|\).
For convex \(F\), the exact subdifferential residual may be written \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial(F+\iota_X)(x(z)))\).
special_cases_latex: If a valid lower bound \(L\le F_\star\) is available, \(F(x(z))-L\le\varepsilon\) certifies \(F(x(z))-F_\star\le\varepsilon\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The objective-gap and stationarity certificates are distinct unless assumptions relate stationarity to global suboptimality.
boundary_notes: A stationarity residual does not by itself certify global optimality for a nonconvex objective.
The optimal value or a valid lower bound may be unavailable to individual agents.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimization-progress certificate
Objective-Gap Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point and an independently verified lower bound certify epsilon objective accuracy when their objective-value difference is at most epsilon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F^*=\inf_{z\in\mathbb R^d}F(z)>-\infty\). A pair \((x,\ell)\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-objective-gap certificate if \(x\in\operatorname{dom}F\), \(\ell\) is independently verifiable with \(\ell\le F^*\), and \[F(x)-\ell\le\varepsilon.\] This certificate guarantees \[0\le F(x)-F^*\le\varepsilon.\] In a distributed implementation, \(F(x)\) must aggregate all objective components evaluated at the same candidate \(x\).
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) has finite optimal value \(F^*=\inf_{z\in\mathbb R^d}F(z)\).
A point \(x\in\operatorname{dom}F\) and an independently verifiable scalar lower bound \(\ell\le F^*\) are available.
The requested tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x)-\ell\le\varepsilon\Longrightarrow 0\le F(x)-F^*\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal objective-gap certificate based on an independently verifiable global lower bound; in a distributed implementation, all objective components must be evaluated at the same candidate.

notation.meaning: Global objective and its optimal value
Independently verified lower bound on the optimal value

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Stationarity Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local gradients evaluated at one common point certify smooth stationarity when their average has norm at most epsilon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For positive integers \(m,d\), differentiable functions \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\), and \(F(x)=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x)\), define \[g(x)=\frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m\nabla f_i(x)=\nabla F(x).\] A common point \(x\in\mathbb R^d\), together with the collected local gradients evaluated at \(x\), is an \(\varepsilon\)-smooth-stationarity certificate if \[\|g(x)\|_2\le\varepsilon.\] For \(\varepsilon=0\), this is the first-order stationary condition. Gradients evaluated at different local points do not constitute this certificate without an additional relation to a reported common point.
assumptions_latex: \(m,d\in\mathbb N\) are positive integers, each \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable, and \(F=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\).
Every local gradient is evaluated at the same reported point \(x\in\mathbb R^d\).
The stationarity tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\left\|m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m\nabla f_i(x)\right\|_2\le\varepsilon\Longleftrightarrow\|\nabla F(x)\|_2\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order stationarity certificate for an unconstrained smooth finite-sum objective at a common network point.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Mismatch Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without additional geometry, a vanishing gradient need not imply a small objective gap; arctangent supplies a concrete smooth counterexample.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be \(f(x)=\arctan x\), so \(f'(x)=1/(1+x^2)\) and \(f^*=\inf_x f(x)=-\pi/2\). For \(x_k=k\), \[|f'(x_k)|=\frac1{1+k^2}\longrightarrow0,\qquad f(x_k)-f^*=\arctan(k)+\frac\pi2\longrightarrow\pi.\] Thus arbitrarily accurate smooth-stationarity certificates can coexist with an objective gap bounded away from zero. Converting stationarity into objective accuracy therefore requires additional structure, such as convexity together with suitable growth information, an error bound, or a Polyak–Łojasiewicz inequality.
assumptions_latex: Stationarity is measured only by \(|f'(x)|\).
No convexity, error bound, or Polyak–Łojasiewicz inequality is assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|f'(x_k)|\to0\) while \(f(x_k)-\inf_x f(x)\to\pi\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete boundary showing that smooth stationarity alone does not certify global objective accuracy.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The arctangent counterexample is mathematically correct and the failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but the cited introductory section does not specifically identify this counterexample or the stated limiting objective gap. A source with a locator supporting the failure phenomenon or this example is required.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph with \(|V|=n\), let each agent hold \(x_i\in\mathbb R^d\), stack \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), and define \(\bar x=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\). Let \(B\) be an oriented incidence matrix of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite connected undirected networks with Euclidean agent states; weighted and directed variants require modified operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A network-agreement certificate system is a nonnegative map \(C_{\mathrm{agr}}:(\mathbb R^d)^n\to[0,+\infty)\) whose zero set is the consensus subspace \(\mathcal C=\{\mathbf1\otimes u:u\in\mathbb R^d\}\). Two canonical certificates are \(C_{\mathrm{edge}}(x)=\|(B^\top\otimes I_d)x\|\) and \(C_{\mathrm{dev}}(x)=\|x-\mathbf1\otimes\bar x\|\). For connected \(G\), each is zero if and only if \(x_1=\cdots=x_n\). An \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{agr}}\)-agreement certificate is the inequality \(C_{\mathrm{agr}}(x)\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{agr}}\), with the norm and normalization fixed before comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A network-agreement certificate is a nonnegative residual that vanishes exactly when all agents hold the same vector. It can measure disagreements across graph edges using the incidence matrix or deviations from the network average. On a connected undirected graph, either residual is zero precisely at consensus. An approximate certificate reports that the selected residual is at most a declared tolerance; its meaning depends on the specified norm and normalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For connected \(G\), \(C_{\mathrm{edge}}(x)=0\Longleftrightarrow C_{\mathrm{dev}}(x)=0\Longleftrightarrow x\in\mathcal C\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(L=BB^\top\) is the graph Laplacian, then \(C_{\mathrm{edge}}(x)^2=x^\top(L\otimes I_d)x\).
special_cases_latex: For scalar states, \(d=1\), the edge residual aggregates squared endpoint differences when the Euclidean norm is used.
immediate_consequences_latex: A small edge residual controls deviation from consensus through the graph spectral gap, but the numerical constant depends on \(G\).
boundary_notes: Disconnected graphs certify only componentwise agreement.
Directed graphs generally require a directed incidence, mixing, or weighted-average convention.
review_flags: The supplied graph-consensus hints were not inspected at a locator establishing this exact certificate formulation.
knowledge_statements.title: Network-agreement certificate
Consensus-Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The distance of stacked agent states from the consensus subspace certifies aggregate disagreement and vanishes exactly at consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For positive integers \(m,d\) and stacked states \(X=[x_1^\top;\ldots;x_m^\top]\in\mathbb R^{m\times d}\), define \[R_{\rm con}(X)=(I-J)X,\qquad J=\frac1m\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top.\] An \(\varepsilon\)-consensus-residual certificate satisfies \[\|R_{\rm con}(X)\|_F\le\varepsilon.\] The residual obeys \[\|R_{\rm con}(X)\|_F^2=\sum_{i=1}^m\|x_i-\bar x\|_2^2,\qquad R_{\rm con}(X)=0\Longleftrightarrow x_1=\cdots=x_m.\]
assumptions_latex: \(m,d\in\mathbb N\) are positive integers, and \(X=[x_1^\top;\ldots;x_m^\top]\in\mathbb R^{m\times d}\) stacks the agent states.
\(J=m^{-1}\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\) is the orthogonal projector onto the consensus subspace.
The agreement tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|(I-J)X\|_Feevaluate\le\varepsilon\), with \((I-J)X=0\Longleftrightarrow x_1=\cdots=x_m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean network-agreement certificate using orthogonal distance to the consensus subspace.

knowledge_statements.title: Disagreement-Energy Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Laplacian quadratic form equals weighted edge disagreement and, on a connected graph, vanishes exactly when every agent agrees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a connected undirected weighted graph \(G=(V,E,w)\) with \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), symmetric nonnegative weights \((w_{ij})\), Laplacian \(L\), and stacked states \(X=[x_1^\top;\ldots;x_m^\top]\), define \[\mathcal E_G(X)=\operatorname{tr}(X^\top L X)=\frac12\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^m w_{ij}\|x_i-x_j\|_2^2.\] An \(\varepsilon\)-disagreement-energy certificate satisfies \[\mathcal E_G(X)\le\varepsilon^2.\] For a connected graph, the exact-zero relation is \[\mathcal E_G(X)=0\Longleftrightarrow x_1=\cdots=x_m.\]
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E,w)\) is a connected undirected weighted graph with \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), nonnegative symmetric weights \(w_{ij}=w_{ji}\), and Laplacian \(L\).
\(d\in\mathbb N\) is positive, and \(X=[x_1^\top;\ldots;x_m^\top]\in\mathbb R^{m\times d}\) stacks the vertex states.
The energy tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal E_G(X)=\operatorname{tr}(X^\top L X)=\frac12\sum_{i,j=1}^m w_{ij}\|x_i-x_j\|_2^2\), with \(\mathcal E_G(X)=0\Longleftrightarrow x_1=\cdots=x_m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Laplacian quadratic-form certificate for agreement over a connected undirected weighted network.

knowledge_statements.title: Pairwise-Discrepancy Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every edge discrepancy is at most epsilon, every pairwise discrepancy is at most graph diameter times epsilon; zero edge discrepancy is global consensus on a connected graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite connected undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\) and states \(x_i\in\mathbb R^d\), define \[\delta_E(X)=\max_{\{i,j\}\in E}\|x_i-x_j\|_2.\] An \(\varepsilon\)-pairwise-discrepancy certificate satisfies \[\delta_E(X)\le\varepsilon.\] For all vertices \(u,v\in V\), it guarantees \[\|x_u-x_v\|_2\le d_G(u,v)\varepsilon\le D\varepsilon,\] where \(d_G\) is shortest-path distance and \(D\) is the graph diameter. Its exact-zero relation is \[\delta_E(X)=0\Longleftrightarrow x_u=x_v\quad\text{for all }u,v\in V.\]
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a connected undirected graph with finite vertex set \(V\).
For a positive integer \(d\), every vertex \(i\in V\) holds a state \(x_i\in\mathbb R^d\), and every edge can report the norm of its endpoint-state difference.
The discrepancy tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta_E(X)\le\varepsilon\Longrightarrow\|x_u-x_v\|_2\le d_G(u,v)\varepsilon\le D\varepsilon\) for all \(u,v\in V\), with \(\delta_E(X)=0\Longleftrightarrow x_u=x_v\) for all \(u,v\in V\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Edgewise maximum-norm agreement certificate on a finite connected undirected graph.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-to-Global Agreement Relations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The graph spectral gap converts disagreement energy into distance from consensus, while the variance identity converts consensus residual into total pairwise discrepancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E,w)\) be a connected undirected weighted graph with \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), Laplacian \(L\), and \(\lambda_2(L)>0\). For \(X=[x_1^\top;\ldots;x_m^\top]\in\mathbb R^{m\times d}\) and \(J=m^{-1}\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\), the local-to-global agreement relations are \[\lambda_2(L)\|(I-J)X\|_F^2\le\operatorname{tr}(X^\top L X),\qquad \sum_{1\le i<j\le m}\|x_i-x_j\|_2^2=m\|(I-J)X\|_F^2.\] In particular, \[\operatorname{tr}(X^\top L X)\le\eta\Longrightarrow\|(I-J)X\|_F\le\sqrt{\eta/\lambda_2(L)}\] for every \(\eta\ge0\).
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E,w)\) is a connected undirected weighted graph with \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), Laplacian \(L\), and spectral gap \(\lambda_2(L)>0\).
\(d\in\mathbb N\) is positive, \(X=[x_1^\top;\ldots;x_m^\top]\in\mathbb R^{m\times d}\), and \(J=m^{-1}\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_2(L)\|(I-J)X\|_F^2\le\operatorname{tr}(X^\top L X)\) and \(\sum_{1\le i<j\le m}\|x_i-x_j\|_2^2=m\|(I-J)X\|_F^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral and variance relations converting local graph disagreement into global consensus and all-pairs bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupling-Feasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local set-distance residuals and the aggregate affine-coupling residual certify how closely the reported distributed variables satisfy all local and coupling constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m\ge1\), let \(x_i\in\mathbb R^{d_i}\) be the vector reported by agent \(i\), and let the required local and coupling constraints be \(x_i\in X_i\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^mA_ix_i=b\), where \(b\in\mathbb R^p\). For tolerances \(\varepsilon_i\ge0\) and \(\varepsilon_c\ge0\), the tuple \((x_1,\ldots,x_m)\) has a coupling-feasibility certificate when
\[\operatorname{dist}(x_i,X_i)\le\varepsilon_i\quad(i=1,\ldots,m),\qquad \left\|\sum_{i=1}^mA_ix_i-b\right\|\le\varepsilon_c.\]
These residual inequalities certify exact feasibility when every tolerance is zero and feasibility to the displayed tolerances otherwise.
assumptions_latex: \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{d_i}\) is nonempty and closed for every \(i\).
\(A_i:\mathbb R^{d_i}\to\mathbb R^p\) is linear for every \(i\).
The distance and residual norm are evaluated using fixed norms on the relevant finite-dimensional spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x_i,X_i)\le\varepsilon_i\) for every \(i\) and \(\|\sum_{i=1}^mA_ix_i-b\|\le\varepsilon_c\) certify feasibility to the stated tolerances; zero tolerances certify exact feasibility.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual certificate for affine coupling constraints in a separable distributed problem.

notation.meaning: distance from a point to a set

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let agent variables satisfy \(x_i\in X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{d_i}\). Let the global coupling constraints be \(\sum_{i=1}^n A_i x_i=b\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^n g_i(x_i)\le0\), with the vector inequality interpreted componentwise.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional distributed problems with separable local domains and affine or nonlinear global coupling constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), define the local-domain residual \(r_X(x)=(\operatorname{dist}(x_i,X_i))_{i=1}^n\), the equality residual \(r_{=}(x)=\sum_iA_ix_i-b\), and the inequality violation \(r_{\le}(x)=[\sum_i g_i(x_i)]_+\), where \([u]_+\) is componentwise positive part. A coupling-feasibility certificate is a declared aggregate \(C_{\mathrm{feas}}(x)=\Phi(r_X(x),r_{=}(x),r_{\le}(x))\ge0\), where \(\Phi\) is zero exactly when all its residual arguments are zero. The point is exactly feasible if \(C_{\mathrm{feas}}(x)=0\), and is \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\)-feasible if \(C_{\mathrm{feas}}(x)\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coupling-feasibility certificate combines residuals for local-set membership, global equalities, and global inequalities. Equality violation is the norm of the aggregate mismatch; inequality violation is the positive part of the aggregate constraint function. The aggregation rule must be nonnegative and vanish only when every included residual vanishes. Exact zero therefore means satisfaction of every represented constraint, while a tolerance defines approximate feasibility under the declared scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_{\mathrm{feas}}(x)=0\) if and only if \(x_i\in X_i\) for every \(i\), \(\sum_iA_ix_i=b\), and \(\sum_i g_i(x_i)\le0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: A weighted sum of the three nonnegative residual norms has the same zero set when all weights are strictly positive.
special_cases_latex: With only a resource-balance equality, the certificate reduces to \(\|\sum_iA_ix_i-b\|\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Changing residual weights preserves exact feasibility but changes the meaning of an approximate tolerance.
boundary_notes: Feasibility does not certify objective optimality or network consensus.
For conic constraints, positive part must be replaced by distance to the relevant cone.

notation.meaning: componentwise maximum of u and zero
residual aggregation map with a singleton zero set at zero residuals

knowledge_statements.title: Coupling-feasibility certificate
Primal-Dual Gap Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible primal point and a dual point with a finite, evaluable dual value yield a nonnegative gap; a gap at most epsilon certifies both primal suboptimality and dual lower-bound error at most epsilon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m\ge1\), let \(x=(x_1,ldots,x_m)\), and define \(P(x)=\sum_{i=1}^mf_i(x_i)\) subject to \(x_i\in X_i\) and \(Ax=\sum_{i=1}^mA_ix_i=b\), where \(A_i:\mathbb R^{d_i}\to\mathbb R^p\) is linear and \(b\in\mathbb R^p\). For \(y\in\mathbb R^p\), define
\[D(y)=\inf_{z_i\in X_i}\left\{\sum_{i=1}^mf_i(z_i)+\left\langle y,\sum_{i=1}^mA_iz_i-b\right\rangle\right\}.\]
For a primal-feasible \(x\) and a dual vector \(y\) for which \(D(y)\) is finite and available, the gap \(G(x,y)=P(x)-D(y)\) is nonnegative. For any \(\varepsilon\ge0\), the inequality \(G(x,y)\le\varepsilon\) certifies both \(P(x)-P^\star\le\varepsilon\) and \(P^\star-D(y)\le\varepsilon\).
assumptions_latex: For every \(i\), \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{d_i}\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(f_i:\mathbb R^{d_i}\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper and convex.
The primal optimal value \(P^\star\) is finite.
The reported \(x\) is primal feasible, and the selected \(y\) satisfies \(D(y)\in\mathbb R\).
The value \(D(y)\) is available to the certificate evaluator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(G(x,y)\le\varepsilon\), then \(0\le P(x)-P^\star\le G(x,y)\le\varepsilon\) and \(0\le P^\star-D(y)\le G(x,y)\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-duality certificate for a convex distributed primal-dual pair.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider a convex primal problem with value \(p_\star=\inf_{x\in X} f(x)\) and a concave dual problem with value \(d_\star=\sup_{y\in Y} q(y)\), where weak duality \(q(y)\le f(x)\) holds for every primal-feasible \(x\) and dual-feasible \(y\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex primal-dual optimization with feasible primal and dual candidates and weak duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a primal-feasible \(x\in X\) and dual-feasible \(y\in Y\), the primal-dual gap certificate is \(G(x,y)=f(x)-q(y)\ge0\). The pair is \(\varepsilon\)-certified when \(G(x,y)\le\varepsilon\). This single inequality certifies both \(0\le f(x)-p_\star\le\varepsilon\) and \(0\le d_\star-q(y)\le\varepsilon\). For a convex-concave saddle function \(L:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\), the restricted saddle gap is \(G_{X,Y}(x,y)=\sup_{v\in Y}L(x,v)-\inf_{u\in X}L(u,y)\), whenever these extrema are finite; it is an exact certificate when its zero set equals the saddle-point set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For feasible primal and dual candidates, the primal-dual gap is the primal objective value minus the dual objective value. Weak duality makes it nonnegative. If the gap is at most a tolerance, the primal candidate is at most that far above the primal optimum and the dual candidate is at most that far below the dual optimum. In a saddle formulation, the corresponding certificate is the worst primal-versus-dual discrepancy over the declared comparison sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G(x,y)\le\varepsilon\Longrightarrow f(x)-p_\star\le\varepsilon\) and \(d_\star-q(y)\le\varepsilon\).
special_cases_latex: At \(\varepsilon=0\), feasible \(x,y\) are primal and dual optimal whenever the gap is zero.
immediate_consequences_latex: A computable feasible dual value supplies a lower bound on the primal optimum.
boundary_notes: An infeasible candidate requires additional feasibility residuals; the raw objective difference alone is not a valid gap certificate.
Restricted saddle gaps depend on the comparison sets and may be infinite on unbounded domains.

children.title: Distributed Stopping Criteria
children.top_down_role: Termination evidence available without complete global state.

knowledge_statements.title: Locally Checkable Stopping Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent checks neighbor disagreement and its local KKT residual; unanimous acceptance certifies bounded global edge disagreement and componentwise stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected communication graph, and let agent \(i\) know \(x_i\), \(g_i\in\partial f_i(x_i)\), and its neighbors' iterates. A locally checkable stopping certificate at tolerances \((\varepsilon_c,\varepsilon_s)\) consists of local inequalities
\[\max_{j:\{i,j\}\in E}\|x_i-x_j\|\le\varepsilon_c,\qquad \left\|g_i+\sum_{j:\{i,j\}\in E}(\lambda_{ij}-\lambda_{ji})\right\|\le\varepsilon_s\]
for every agent, using exchanged edge multipliers \(\lambda_{ij}\). Acceptance by every agent certifies the displayed edge-consensus and local KKT-stationarity residual bounds without collecting the complete global state.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is connected and undirected.
Each \(f_i\) is proper and convex.
Adjacent agents can authenticate the iterates and edge multipliers used in their checks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All edge disagreements are at most \(\varepsilon_c\), and every local KKT-stationarity residual is at most \(\varepsilon_s\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Neighbor-local termination certificate for consensus and stationarity residuals.

notation.meaning: directed copy of an edge multiplier

review_flags: A precise authoritative source for this particular locally checkable KKT certificate is required.
standard_field_rationale: neighbor-wise consensus and componentwise KKT residuals are standard distributed termination tests.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits the leaf, but no citation is supplied and the directed multiplier expression is not tied to a precisely oriented consensus constraint system or an edge-consistency condition. Those choices affect whether the displayed residual is a valid local KKT residual, so an authoritative source and exact formulation are required.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a communication graph. At a candidate stopping time \(t\), agent \(i\) observes a local view \(v_i^t\), containing its state and only information admitted from its neighborhood or message history.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributed termination with bounded local views and an explicitly specified global accuracy predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A locally checkable stopping-certificate system for a global predicate \(P_\varepsilon(z^t)\) consists of local certificate maps \(c_i:\mathcal V_i\to[0,+\infty)\), local thresholds \(\tau_i\ge0\), and an aggregation predicate \(A\) such that soundness holds: for every admissible global state \(z^t\), \(A(c_1(v_1^t)\le\tau_1,\ldots,c_n(v_n^t)\le\tau_n)=\mathrm{true}\) implies \(P_\varepsilon(z^t)\). It is complete for a class \(\mathcal S\) if \(P_\varepsilon(z)\) implies acceptance for every \(z\in\mathcal S\). It is fully local when each \(c_i\) depends only on \(v_i^t\), not on the complete global state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally checkable stopping certificate assigns each agent a test based solely on its allowed local view. A declared aggregation rule combines those tests. The system is sound if collective acceptance always implies the specified global accuracy property. Completeness is a separate requirement: every sufficiently accurate state in a declared class must also be accepted. Local checkability concerns information access, not merely whether the residual decomposes algebraically.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Collective local acceptance is a valid stopping decision only when it implies \(P_\varepsilon(z^t)\) for every admissible state.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For conjunctive aggregation, acceptance is \(\max_i c_i(v_i^t)/\tau_i\le1\), with zero-threshold cases treated separately.
special_cases_latex: A radius-one certificate uses only an agent's state and the most recently received states of its graph neighbors.
immediate_consequences_latex: Soundness prevents premature termination; completeness controls failure to terminate after the target property holds.
boundary_notes: Simultaneous local tests may be unsound under stale or inconsistent snapshots unless the admissible-state model accounts for them.
A centralized computation of local residuals is not locally checkable in the information-theoretic sense.

notation.meaning: information locally available to agent i at time t

children.title: Distributed Optimization Benchmark and Baseline Design

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_query: A Field Guide to Federated Optimization

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(a\in\mathcal A\) denote a distributed optimization method and \(e\in\mathcal E\) an evaluation environment. Let \(Z(a,e,\omega)\) be the resulting execution trace under randomness \(\omega\), and let \(V(Z)\in\mathbb R^q\) collect optimization error, communication, computation, latency, participation, topology, and fault measurements. A comparison rule is a map \(C:\mathbb R^q\times\mathbb R^q\to\{-1,0,1,\bot\}\), where \(\bot\) denotes noncomparability.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite experimental or simulated evaluations of distributed optimization. The definition formalizes when a reported ordering is unsupported because deployment-relevant coordinates or normalization constraints are absent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a target deployment class \(\mathcal D\subseteq\mathcal E\), an evaluation specification is \(E=(e,M,B,N)\), where \(M\subseteq\{1,\ldots,q\}\) is the set of reported metric coordinates, \(B\) is the declared resource-budget constraint, and \(N\) is the normalization rule. Given methods \(a,b\), the specification crosses a distributed evaluation boundary relative to \(\mathcal D\) when it reports a strict ordering \(C(V(Z(a,e)),V(Z(b,e)))\in\{-1,1\}\), but at least one of the following holds: \(e
otin\mathcal D\); a deployment-relevant coordinate lies outside \(M\); the executions violate the common constraint \(B\); or \(N\) maps unequal resources, participation laws, or network conditions to the same comparison scale. Formally, with \(R(\mathcal D)\subseteq\{1,\ldots,q\}\) denoting relevant coordinates, the boundary condition is \[e
otin\mathcal D\ \lor\ R(\mathcal D)
subseteq M\ \lor\ Z(a,e)
otin B\ \lor\ Z(b,e)
otin B\ \lor\ 
eg\operatorname{Invariant}_{\mathcal D}(N).\] A comparison is admissible only if none of these disjuncts holds and the uncertainty specification attached to every stochastic reported coordinate is defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributed evaluation boundary is crossed when an experiment ranks two methods even though its environment is outside the target deployment class, it omits a deployment-relevant metric, it gives the methods incompatible budgets, or its normalization conceals unequal resources, participation, or network conditions. An admissible comparison must remain inside the deployment class, report all relevant coordinates, enforce a common budget, use a deployment-invariant normalization, and specify uncertainty for stochastic measurements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The evaluation \(E\) is boundary-valid for \(a,b\) relative to \(\mathcal D\) iff \(e\in\mathcal D\), \(R(\mathcal D)\subseteq M\), both traces satisfy \(B\), \(\operatorname{Invariant}_{\mathcal D}(N)\) holds, and stochastic coordinates carry an uncertainty specification.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Define \(Q(E,a,b;\mathcal D)\) as the conjunction of environment fidelity, metric completeness, budget parity, normalization invariance, and uncertainty specification. Then boundary validity is \(Q=1\), while a reported ordering with \(Q=0\) is boundary-crossing.
special_cases_latex: Communication-round-only reporting is the case in which \(M\) excludes message volume, latency, or local computation despite their relevance to \(\mathcal D\).
Topology-agnostic comparison occurs when \(N\) or the report suppresses deployment-relevant graph parameters.
immediate_consequences_latex: A scalar ranking is not defined by this criterion when two methods trade off different relevant resource coordinates without an explicit scalarization.
Results obtained outside \(\mathcal D\) may remain descriptive of the tested environment but do not constitute a deployment-valid ordering.
boundary_notes: The definition does not prescribe which metrics are relevant; \(R(\mathcal D)\) must be declared from the deployment requirements.
It does not require every experiment to emulate every deployment, only that conclusions be scoped to the represented deployment class.

children.title: Communication, Computation, and Wall-Clock Cost Reporting
children.top_down_role: Efficiency evaluation omitting message size, latency, or local work.

knowledge_statements.title: Communication-Round-Only Evaluation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equal communication-round counts do not imply equal bandwidth, runtime, or local computation when per-round messages and work are unconstrained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an execution with \(R\) rounds, total communicated bits are \(B=\sum_{r=1}^R b_r\) and total local work is \(C=\sum_{r=1}^R c_r\). Fixing \(R\) places no finite upper bound on either \(B\) or \(C\) when \(b_r\) and \(c_r\) are unrestricted. Two methods can therefore have the same round count while one transmits arbitrarily larger messages or performs arbitrarily more local oracle calls. Consequently a communication-round-only evaluation supports a resource comparison only after common bounds or measurements for message size, latency, participation, and local work are supplied.
assumptions_latex: Evaluation reports only the number \(R\) of synchronous communication rounds.
Message size, latency, local oracle calls, and local arithmetic are unreported.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Round count alone cannot order total communication, wall-clock time, or computation without additional per-round resource bounds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource-accounting boundary for comparisons based exclusively on synchronous round count.
review_flags: The supplied communication-aspects locator is relevant but does not specifically support the stated evaluation failure boundary.

children.title: Participation and Availability Scenario Reporting
children.top_down_role: Experiments using availability patterns unlike the target deployment.

knowledge_statements.title: Unrealistic Participation Evaluation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluation under the wrong participation law can have maximal bias; full-participation experiments cannot certify deployment performance when full participation never occurs there.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z_t\subseteq [m]\) be the clients participating at round \(t\), and let \(P\) and \(Q\) denote the deployment and experimental laws of \(Z_{1:T}\), respectively. For every measurable performance loss \(L(Z_{1:T})\in[0,1]\), \[\left|\mathbb E_P[L]-\mathbb E_Q[L]\right|\leq d_{\mathrm{TV}}(P,Q),\qquad \sup_{0\leq L\leq1}\left|\mathbb E_P[L]-\mathbb E_Q[L]\right|=d_{\mathrm{TV}}(P,Q).\] Hence an evaluation is participation-unrealistic beyond tolerance \(\varepsilon\) when \(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(P,Q)>\varepsilon\). In particular, if \(Q(Z_t=[m]\ \forall t)=1\) while \(P(Z_t=[m]\ \forall t)=0\), then \(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(P,Q)=1\), so experimental performance gives no distribution-free guarantee for deployment performance.
assumptions_latex: \(m,T\in\mathbb N\) and \(Z_t\subseteq[m]\).
\(P\) and \(Q\) are probability laws on the same participation-sequence space.
\(L\) is measurable and takes values in \([0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(P,Q)>\varepsilon\) permits evaluation bias exceeding \(\varepsilon\), and mutually exclusive participation regimes permit bias \(1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distribution-shift boundary for client-availability patterns in finite-horizon distributed evaluations.

notation.meaning: Set of clients participating at round t.
Total-variation distance, using the supremum-over-events convention.

children.title: Topology-Controlled Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Comparisons concealing differences in network conditioning.

knowledge_statements.title: Topology-Agnostic Comparison
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equal round counts conceal unequal mixing: one topology may average exactly while another retains nearly all disagreement after the same communication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathbf 1\in\mathbb R^m\) be the all-ones vector, let \(J=\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}/m\), and let \(I_m\) be the \(m\times m\) identity matrix. For a symmetric doubly stochastic matrix \(W\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\), define \(\rho(W)=\lVert W-J\rVert_2<1\). For every \(k\in\mathbb N_0\), after \(k\) pure mixing rounds, disagreement satisfies \[\lVert W^k-J\rVert_2=\rho(W)^k.\] Thus equal communication-round counts across networks are not comparable unless \(W\), \(\rho(W)\), or an equivalent spectral-gap normalization is reported and controlled. For \(W_\alpha=(1-\alpha)I_m+\alpha J\) with \(0<\alpha<1\), \(\rho(W_\alpha)=1-\alpha\), whereas \(\rho(J)=0\). Consequently, one round gives exact averaging under \(J\) but leaves a fraction \(1-\alpha\) of worst-case disagreement under \(W_\alpha\).
assumptions_latex: \(W\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is symmetric and doubly stochastic, and \(\lVert W-J\rVert_2<1\).
One communication round applies the mixing operator \(W\) once.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Communication rounds are topology-dependent resources because disagreement contracts by \(\rho(W)^k\), not by a topology-independent function of \(k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of round-count comparisons that omit the contraction quality of network mixing.

notation.meaning: Orthogonal averaging matrix onto the consensus subspace.
Spectral contraction factor on the disagreement subspace.

children.title: Centralized and Distributed Baseline Budget Matching
children.top_down_role: Comparisons using inconsistent oracle, batch, or computation budgets.

knowledge_statements.title: Centralized-Baseline Budget Mismatch
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equal iteration counts are unfair when the distributed method receives more oracle calls, samples, or aggregate computation than the centralized baseline.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an execution through round \(K\), define total oracle cost \(C_{\mathrm{orc}}=\sum_{t=1}^K\sum_{i=1}^m q_{i,t}\) and total local computation \(C_{\mathrm{comp}}=\sum_{t=1}^K\sum_{i=1}^m c_{i,t}\), where inactive workers contribute zero. A centralized–distributed comparison is budget-mismatched if it reports performance at equal \(K\) while either \(C_{\mathrm{orc}}\) or \(C_{\mathrm{comp}}\) differs and the difference is not separately controlled. In particular, if each of \(m\) workers evaluates a batch of size \(b\) per round, the distributed method uses \(Kmb\) sample-oracle calls; a centralized baseline using one batch of size \(b\) uses only \(Kb\). Their equal-round comparison therefore differs by an oracle-budget factor of \(m\).
assumptions_latex: \(K,m,b\in\mathbb N\).
\(q_{i,t}\) and \(c_{i,t}\) count oracle calls and local computation for worker \(i\) at round \(t\).
Compared oracle calls have the same information content and unit cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equal-round results do not isolate algorithmic performance when total oracle or computation budgets differ; the batch example has ratio \(Kmb/(Kb)=m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource-accounting boundary for centralized and distributed optimization comparisons.

notation.meaning: Total number of sample-oracle calls across all workers.
Total local computation accumulated across workers.
Number of reported optimization rounds or iterations.

children.title: Distributed Optimization Reproducibility and Statistical Reporting

knowledge_statements.title: Random-Seed and Independent-Trial Reporting
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Report the trial count, seeds or their generation rule, and all resampled randomness; do not treat repeated measurements of one run as independent trials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an algorithm, dataset partition, participation rule, hyperparameters, and evaluation protocol. For trials \(r=1,\ldots,R\), let \(s_r\) identify the random stream and let \(Y_r=M(s_r)\) be the resulting trial-level metric. A complete trial report states \(R\), every \(s_r\) or a deterministic seed-generation rule, and which random objects are resampled. A claim that trials are independent requires the model \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_R\) to be independent conditional on the fixed experimental configuration; merely changing integer seed labels does not establish this property. Repeated measurements from one trained run must not be counted as independent trials.
assumptions_latex: The experimental configuration is fixed before comparing trial outcomes.
Each trial produces a well-defined scalar metric \(Y_r\).
Any independence claim is conditional on the fixed configuration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The report identifies \(R\), the streams \(s_1,\ldots,s_R\), the resampling unit, and whether \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_R\) are modeled as independent.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reproducibility requirement for stochastic distributed-optimization experiments.

notation.meaning: Seed or random-stream identifier for trial r.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits the reporting topic and distinguishes independent trials from repeated measurements, but its mandatory reporting fields and conditional-independence standard have no supporting statistical or reproducibility citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Uncertainty and Across-Trial Variability Reporting
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Report the estimand, trial count, across-trial standard deviation, and uncertainty method; distinguish variability among trials from uncertainty in their mean, and state the assumptions used for any confidence interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For independent trial-level measurements \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_R\) with finite variance and \(R\ge2\), report the estimand and compute \(\bar Y=R^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^R Y_r\), \(s^2=(R-1)^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^R(Y_r-\bar Y)^2\), and \(\operatorname{SE}(\bar Y)=s/\sqrt R\) when the sample mean is the estimator. Any reported interval must identify its construction and confidence level. If \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_R\) are independent and identically distributed as \(\mathcal N(\mu,\sigma^2)\), with unknown \(\mu\) and \(\sigma^2\), then for \(0<\alpha<1\) the two-sided \((1-\alpha)\)-level confidence interval for \(\mu\) is \(\bar Y\pm t_{R-1,1-\alpha/2}s/\sqrt R\). The standard deviation and standard error must be labeled distinctly.
assumptions_latex: The values \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_R\) are trial-level rather than within-trial repeated measurements.
The measurements are independent, have finite variance, and satisfy \(R\ge2\).
The displayed Student interval additionally assumes \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_R\) are identically distributed normal measurements with a common unknown mean and variance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The report provides \(R\), \(\bar Y\), \(s\), and a labeled uncertainty measure whose construction, assumptions, and confidence level are stated.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trial-level uncertainty summaries for a scalar distributed-optimization metric.

notation.meaning: Sample mean and across-trial sample standard deviation.
Estimated standard error of the sample mean.
The p-quantile of the Student t distribution with nu degrees of freedom.

knowledge_statements.title: Hardware and Software Environment Reporting
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Record versioned hardware, runtime, drivers, libraries, communication backend, precision, and determinism settings, together with the criterion used to judge reproduced outputs equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent the execution environment by \(E=(H,O,R,D,L,C)\), recording hardware topology and accelerators, operating system, language runtime, drivers, versioned libraries, and compiler or build settings. A reproducibility report states \(E\), the distributed communication backend, numerical precision, and determinism settings. For original output \(x\) and reproduced output \(x'\), it must also declare an equivalence predicate, such as \(x\sim_\varepsilon x'\) exactly when \(d(x,x')\le\varepsilon\), or a distributional comparison for stochastic runs. Performance comparisons intended to isolate algorithms must hold relevant components of \(E\) fixed or model them explicitly as experimental factors.
assumptions_latex: Every reported run is associated with an identifiable execution environment \(E\).
The output space has a declared comparison rule, such as a metric \(d\).
Any cross-environment performance claim identifies which environmental components vary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The report specifies \(E\) and a reproducibility relation such as \(x\sim_\varepsilon x'\iff d(x,x')\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Execution-environment disclosure and reproducibility equivalence for distributed experiments.

notation.meaning: Tuple describing the execution hardware and software environment.
Declared tolerance-based equivalence of original and reproduced outputs.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits the environment-reporting topic and its notation is internally consistent, but no standard or protocol source supports the asserted mandatory environment fields or the requirement to declare the proposed output-equivalence predicate.

knowledge_statements.title: Dataset, Partition, and Participation Reporting
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete reporting identifies the processed dataset, reconstructs every trial’s agent partition, and records or reproducibly generates the round-by-round participation pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the processed dataset be \(D=\{z_j\}_{j=1}^{N}\), let \(D_i^{(r)}\subseteq D\) denote the data assigned to agent \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) in trial \(r\), and let \(a_{i,t}^{(r)}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate participation at round \(t\). Dataset, partition, and participation reporting is complete if it specifies: the dataset version, inclusion rules, and preprocessing; the partition-generating rule, its parameters and random seed, together with every \(|D_i^{(r)}|\); and either the realized array \((a_{i,t}^{(r)})\) or a fully specified sampling or dropout law with its parameters and seed. These disclosures must determine each trial's processed data allocation and participation sequence up to explicitly identified nondeterminism.
assumptions_latex: The experiment has finitely many agents, trials, and communication rounds.
Each processed example has a stable identifier or an equivalent reproducible ordering.
All unreported nondeterminism is explicitly identified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reported information determines \(D\), every family \((D_i^{(r)})_{i=1}^{m}\), and every participation array \((a_{i,t}^{(r)})_{i,t}\), except for declared nondeterminism.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum reproducibility condition for data allocation and time-varying agent participation in a distributed optimization experiment.

notation.meaning: Processed data assigned to agent i in trial r.
Indicator that agent i participates at round t of trial r.

REQUEST_SOURCES: add an authoritative distributed or federated learning experimental-reporting standard.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The content kind “condition” fits this reporting leaf, and the LaTeX delimiters are safe. However, the record has no source reference or inspectable locator, while the supplied inventory concerns distributed-optimization algorithms rather than experimental-reporting standards. Source support is therefore required for this normative completeness criterion. In addition, the domains of trial r and round t are not explicitly defined, and reporting only dataset version, inclusion rules, preprocessing, partition parameters, sizes, and a seed does not necessarily determine the exact processed dataset D or every allocation unless exact data snapshots/identifiers, implementation details, and deterministic seed semantics are also specified. The authoritative source should establish the intended disclosure standard before those claims are corrected.
